current_activity: attacks at 0400 behind two Panthers and takes Honsfeld by surprise
notes: Event date: 17 December 1944, 0400 (Cole, ch. 11). Event definition: Peiper puts two Panther tanks at the head of an infantry battalion and attacks Honsfeld at 0400; it is taken with ease (Cole, ch. 11). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 11, p. 261: "at 0400 attacked toward Honsfeld". Location: Honsfeld, Büllingen (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Honsfeld. Commander: Colonel (SS-Obersturmbannführer) Joachim Peiper (Cole, ch. 11). Opponents: US 99th Infantry Division.

current_activity: advance guard reaches Stavelot on the Amblève at dusk
notes: Event date: 17 December 1944, dusk (Cole, ch. 11). Event definition: Advancing along the south bank of the Amblève, the advance guard reaches Stavelot, where the river must be crossed, at dusk (Cole, ch. 11). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 11, p. 265: "the advance guard reached Stavelot, the point where the river must be crossed, at dusk". Location: Stavelot, Liège with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Stavelot. Commander: Colonel (SS-Obersturmbannführer) Joachim Peiper (Cole, ch. 11).

current_activity: bulk of the battle group attacks Stoumont, the last exit west along the Amblève
notes: Event date: 19 December 1944 (Cole, ch. 15). Event definition: On 19 December Peiper is engaged with the bulk of his troops in an attempt to blast a path through Stoumont (Cole, ch. 15). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 15, p. 339: "Peiper was engaged with the bulk of his troops in an attempt to blast a path through Stoumont". Location: Stoumont, Liège (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Stoumont. Commander: Colonel (SS-Obersturmbannführer) Joachim Peiper (Cole, ch. 11). Opponents: US 30th Infantry Division (119th Infantry).

current_activity: pulled back from Stoumont into an all-round defense at La Gleize
notes: Event date: night of 21-22 December 1944 (Cole, ch. 16). Event definition: Peiper withdraws his last forces from Stoumont during the night and early morning to fight a last-ditch action at La Gleize (Cole, ch. 16). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 16, p. 373: "Peiper had withdrawn his last forces in Stoumont during the night and early morning". Location: La Gleize, Liège (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names La Gleize. Commander: Colonel (SS-Obersturmbannführer) Joachim Peiper (Cole, ch. 11). Opponents: US 30th Infantry Division.

current_activity: about 800 men break out of La Gleize on foot at 0100, abandoning their vehicles
notes: Event date: 24 December 1944, 0100 (Cole, ch. 16). Event definition: With permission to break out, Peiper and some eight hundred men leave La Gleize at 0100 in single file through the woods, cross the river and by daybreak are in the hills north of Trois-Ponts; a rear guard demolishes the vehicles (Cole, ch. 16). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 16, p. 376: "Peiper and some eight hundred of his command started at 0100 in single file". Location: La Gleize, Liège (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names La Gleize. Commander: Colonel (SS-Obersturmbannführer) Joachim Peiper (Cole, ch. 11).
